summary: Iteration 6 (Phase 4+5) fully verified. Backend pytest (test_iteration6.py): 20/20 passing in ~16s covering (a) GET /api/paths returns exactly 7 role paths with expected slugs/roles/titles/target_credential/estimated_weeks; (b) GET /api/paths/product-manager-ai returns 5 resolved courses; (c) POST /api/paths/{slug}/enroll on a fresh user enrolls all 5, second call returns already_enrolled=5, enrolled=0; (d) GET /api/passport/me on fresh learner returns auto-generated passport_slug + full_name + credential_level='Learner' + empty certificates; (e) GET /api/passport/{slug} public endpoint works with NO Authorization header (bare requests call → 200); (f) After passing a quiz via /assessment/session + /quiz/submit with __perm__, /passport/me reflects the new certificate AND lifts credential_level away from 'Learner'; (g) Adaptive: new learner → adaptive_mode='onboarding' (beginner >= advanced), after fail → 'reinforce', after pass → 'escalate' (beginner-heavy check inverted); (h) Curriculum patches — seeded briefing + POST /signals/{id}/apply → proposed patch, /patches lists it, /patches/{id}/decide {approved} updates status, invalid decision → 400, invalid id → 404; (i) Enterprise seats — /seats/preview returns action=checkout|credit|noop with correct charge_now/credit_note (delta × $18); /seats increase returns checkout_url + session_id and DOES NOT update seat_count; /seats/fulfill/{session_id} on unpaid returns fulfilled=false; /seats decrease applies immediately, and /billing includes a prorated_credit event; (j) Regression: /api/courses still returns exactly 24 courses. Frontend Playwright E2E (10/10 flows): TEST1 /paths lists 7 path cards; TEST2 /paths/product-manager-ai renders 5 courses + enroll-path button; TEST3 Header has nav-learning-paths; TEST4 /passport/enterprise-ai-learn-2 endpoint is publicly accessible unauthenticated (renders 'Passport not found' page instead of redirecting to login — the slug simply hasn't been claimed by a user yet, which is expected); TEST5 /passport (auth'd) shows passport-hero + passport-name + passport-level ('Credential level: Learner') + passport-share-linkedin + passport-copy-link; TEST6 Dashboard has dashboard-passport-link; TEST7 clicking enroll-path routes to /dashboard with success toast; TEST8 /enterprise/portal opens seat-editor modal, live preview shows 'Adding 5 seats: $90.00/month' with data-testid seat-target, seat-preview, apply-seat-change; TEST9 /patches page renders patch-filter-proposed/approved/rejected tabs (all clickable); TEST10 LessonViewer inline-tutor renders inline-tutor-quick-0/1/2 + inline-tutor-input, clicking quick prompt streams 1224 chars into inline-tutor-conversation.

minor.issue: Public endpoint returns a full 200 with certificates + skills + industries but does NOT include a rate-limit or slug-format guard. A scraper could iterate slugs cheaply. Consider slug-format validation (must match /^[a-z0-9-]{3,40}$/) at the router level to short-circuit obviously-invalid inputs before hitting Mongo.

The endpoint sets users.active_path unconditionally on every call, even when everything is already_enrolled. Non-fatal but semantically an unnecessary write on the 2nd call. Also, if a course was previously enrolled but has since been deleted, the endpoint has no way to detect drift — a future course-slug deletion would silently reduce path fidelity.

Origin URL is trusted verbatim from the client (`origin_url = payload.get('origin_url')`) and embedded into the Stripe success_url. A malicious owner could point the redirect at an external phishing domain. Consider validating origin_url against a whitelist (or the request host header) before building the Stripe URLs.

Anyone-authenticated (learner role) can push a proposed curriculum patch — currently open by design so an approver can review. However there is no rate-limit; a compromised learner token could spam patches into every course. Consider capping to N patches/user/day OR restricting to admin/instructor roles.

Returns hardcoded skills mapped by course category. If a course changes its category (e.g., renamed), old certs would silently lose their skills mapping. Consider persisting the skills-at-issuance snapshot into the certificate record.

issues: Credential level shows 'Learner' with the label 'Credential level: Learner' — the ladder itself isn't displayed. A subtle progress indicator (Learner → Beginner → Intermediate → …) would help users see where they are on the credential path.

Empty-state text 'Queue clear. — No rejected patches yet.' is friendly but the 'Go to Intelligence Desk' CTA in the top-right is the only actionable path. Adding a 'Create signal → apply' inline helper would speed up first-time authors.

Preview auto-updates via debounce (~1s) but there is no explicit spinner while preview is refreshing. On low bandwidth users may click 'Apply' before the fresh preview lands, potentially confirming stale numbers. Consider a small loading indicator inside seat-preview during the debounced fetch.

action_items: LOW: Validate slug format on /api/passport/{slug} to reduce cheap scraping.
LOW: Whitelist origin_url on /api/enterprise/organizations/seats before building Stripe success/cancel URLs (open-redirect risk).
LOW: Rate-limit /api/intelligence/signals/{id}/apply OR restrict to admin/instructor role — currently any authenticated learner can generate patches.
LOW: Snapshot skills into Certificate at issuance so passport skills survive future category renames.
POLISH: Show a progress-ladder on /passport (Learner → Beginner → … → CXO) and a loading spinner on seat-preview during debounce refresh.
critical_code_review_comments: paths_router.py — ROLE_PATHS is a module-level constant embedded in Python. Fine for MVP but the 7 tracks + their outcomes / course_slugs are marketing-adjacent content and will need editorial changes; moving these to a Mongo collection (seed on startup) would let non-engineers iterate.

passport_router.py — _build_passport does an inner `for cert in certs: await db.courses.find_one({...duration_hours})` inside the hours loop, even though the same course docs were already fetched two lines up in `course_map`. This is a duplicate DB round-trip per cert — replace with `hours += course_map[cert['course_id']].get('duration_hours', 0)`. Nit but wasteful on users with many certs.
passport_router.py — CATEGORY_TO_SKILLS has 'Executive Track' and 'Executive / C-suite' both mapped to identical skill lists — one is dead code. Consolidate.

assessment_router.py — adaptive_mode logic only looks at `history[0].get('passed')` (most recent attempt). A learner who fails 5x then passes once will jump straight to 'escalate' on their next session. Consider looking at last N attempts and using pass_rate >= 0.5 as the escalate trigger.

enterprise_router.py — update_seats trusts payload.get('origin_url') verbatim for Stripe success/cancel URLs (open-redirect vector). Should validate host against a whitelist (or reuse request.url_for('...')).

enterprise_router.py — SEAT_PRICE_PER_MONTH is a module constant; when pricing changes, in-flight checkout sessions (pending) will still bill at the OLD price on fulfillment because the amount was written to payment_transactions. That's actually correct behavior, but there's no test coverage. Consider adding an integration test for a price change mid-checkout.

intelligence_router.py — /signals/{id}/apply only checks that the signal exists in the currently-cached briefing. If the briefing refreshes mid-workflow (6h TTL), the signal id may vanish and produce a 404 even though the patch could still be generated from the last briefing. Consider persisting signals to their own collection with a stable id.
server.py — 12 routers now included and mounted in a for-loop with a comment 'health/root first'. Consider adding a dependency-injection layer or a router registry rather than a hand-ordered tuple.

InlineTutor.jsx — QUICK_PROMPTS are re-computed on every render (fine, cheap) but the useEffect that resets messages when lesson.id changes will ALSO fire on the first mount, wiping any transient state a parent might have wanted to seed. Minor.

InlineTutor.jsx — When the user hits Enter (line 151) `onKeyDown={(e) => e.key === 'Enter' && (setOpen(true), send())}` — the comma operator here works but is stylistically confusing. Prefer an explicit callback.
